synopsis: ISO 21815-3:2023 is published and provides a directly relevant framework for forward/reverse collision warning and avoidance through speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition—not steering—for earth-moving, mobile underground-mining and road-construction machinery [f2058, f3905, f2163]. Its collision-risk area accounts for detection, decision and action time, machine stopping distance and a residual safety distance; the booklet therefore favors stopping-distance/risk-zone intervention, with time to collision as one input, and machine-scaled scenario geometry [f5911, f6680, f5922, f6770]. Automatic intervention is placed at collision-risk level 4 or above, warning levels must be distinguishable, stronger operator braking must not be overridden, and safe-operation responsibility remains with the operator [f5912, f11723, f5913, f2164]. Old-versus-new comparisons should use common ground truth and a common risk zone, measuring warnings and interventions per hazard, missed hazards, false/nuisance alarms per hour and warning time to collision [f5210, f5479]. The standard does not establish quantified field effectiveness or second-order hazards, and the reviewed standards supply neither statistical acceptance targets nor simulation-credibility rules; Annex D stopping-distance examples are not a validation method, and physical tests remain necessary [f3443, f324, f6749, f7729, f8145]. Important limitations remain: simulation provisions or acceptance of simulation evidence were not found, universal target dimensions and test counts were not found in public abstracts, and only the 2022 draft was reviewed in full, so the published text may differ [f9780, f11237, f5410, f2167].
